definitions.gloss: to make plans; to set up a schedule; to plan ahead
definitions.explanation: To create or arrange a plan or schedule for future activities. The verb {立|た}てる here means to set up or establish.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}の{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てた。
examples.english: I made plans for a trip.

examples.japanese: {来週|らいしゅう}の{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てておこう。
examples.english: Let's go ahead and make plans for next week.

examples.japanese: {早|はや}めに{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てないと、ホテルが{取|と}れなくなる。
examples.english: If we don't plan ahead early, we won't be able to get a hotel.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}が{忙|いそが}しくて、なかなか{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てられない。
examples.english: I'm so busy with work that I can hardly make any plans.

notes:
A common collocation pairing {予定|よてい} ('plan, schedule') with {立|た}てる ('to set up, establish'). This is the standard way to express making plans or setting a schedule in Japanese. The verb {立|た}てる is ichidan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旅行|りょこう}の{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to plan a trip
- {勉強|べんきょう}の{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to make a study plan
- {年間|ねんかん}の{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to set up a yearly schedule
- {無理|むり}のない{予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる: to make a reasonable plan

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {計画|けいかく}を{立|た}てる: to make a plan — more formal and often used for larger, more structured plans
- {日程|にってい}を{決|き}める: to set a schedule — focuses on fixing dates
- {段取|だんど}りをつける: to make arrangements — emphasizes practical preparation steps

USAGE:
In everyday conversation, {予定|よてい}を{立|た}てる is the most natural way to talk about planning. It can refer to anything from casual weekend plans to structured work schedules.
